draft.title: Circles and ellipses
card: A circle is the locus (set of all points) at a fixed distance r from a centre (h, k). Its equation is (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r².
An ellipse centred at (h, k) has equation (x − h)²/a² + (y − k)²/b² = 1. It reaches a units left and right of the centre, and b units up and down.
Read the centre from the brackets, with the signs flipped. In (x + 2)², the centre has x = −2. The numbers under the brackets are squares, so take the square root to get a or b.
Example: (x − 2)²/25 + (y + 1)²/9 = 1 has centre (2, −1), a = 5 and b = 3. So x runs from 2 − 5 = −3 to 2 + 5 = 7.
draft.remember: Brackets give the centre with flipped signs. Squared numbers need a square root.

a.q: What are the centre and radius of the circle (x − 3)² + (y + 4)² = 49?
a.why: The brackets x − 3 and y + 4 give a centre of (3, −4). The right side is r² = 49, so r = 7. Giving a radius of 49 forgets the square root.
a.clue: Flip the signs for the centre, then take a square root.

b.q: What is the greatest x-value on the ellipse (x − 1)²/36 + (y − 2)²/4 = 1?
b.why: The number under the x bracket is 36, so a = 6. The ellipse reaches 6 units right of the centre x = 1, so the greatest x-value is 1 + 6 = 7. The answer 6 forgets to add the centre.
b.clue: Which number belongs to x, and is it a or a²?

final.title: Circles and ellipses
card: A circle is the locus (set of all points) at a fixed distance \(r\) from a centre \((h, k)\). Its equation is \((x - h)^{2} + (y - k)^{2} = r^{2}\).
An ellipse centred at \((h, k)\) has equation \(\frac{(x - h)^{2}}{a^{2}} + \frac{(y - k)^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1\). It reaches \(a\) units left and right of the centre, and \(b\) units up and down.
Read the centre from the brackets, with the signs flipped. In \((x + 2)^{2}\), the centre has \(x = -2\). The numbers under the brackets are squares, so take the square root to get \(a\) or \(b\).
final.remember: Brackets give the centre with flipped signs. Squared numbers need a square root.

a.q: What are the centre and radius of the circle \((x - 3)^{2} + (y + 4)^{2} = 49\)?
a.why: The brackets \(x - 3\) and \(y + 4\) give a centre of \((3, -4)\). The right side is \(r^{2} = 49\), so \(r = 7\). Giving a radius of 49 forgets the square root.
a.clue: Flip the signs for the centre, then take a square root.

b.q: What is the greatest x-value on the ellipse \(\frac{(x - 1)^{2}}{36} + \frac{(y - 2)^{2}}{4} = 1\)?
b.why: The number under the \(x\) bracket is 36, so \(a = 6\). The ellipse reaches 6 units right of the centre \(x = 1\), so the greatest x-value is \(1 + 6 = 7\). The answer 6 forgets to add the centre.
b.clue: Which number belongs to \(x\), and is it \(a\) or \(a^{2}\)?
